Author: Sandro
Name: NahjaUI
Punchline: A complete, modular interface for Final Fantasy XIV.
Description:
NahjaUI gives the game a clean, consistent interface that you build piece by piece. Switch on only what you want: everything else stays exactly as the game made it.

HUD bars: your parameter bar, target, target of target, focus target and party list.
Progress bars: your casts and your target's, with a slidecast marker, plus a global cooldown bar that shows the queue and weave windows.
Job gauges, status effects, nameplates and enmity list, each one with its own style.
Trackers: pick the enhancements, enfeeblements and cooldowns you want to see. Every job comes with ready-made presets.
Profiles: save, copy and share your whole setup.

Type /nui to open it.

Join the testers on Discord: https://nahjaui.github.io/discord
Changelog: Fix: the game could crash, and elements could end up in the wrong place, when elements were attached to each other in a circle (it could happen after the groups of the trackers were merged): the screen limit now breaks those circles, ignores impossible positions, and only works on what hangs from the screen, never on what hangs from another element. Added: every job preset now comes with the central column anchored: the Rotation row fixed in the center, the job gauge under it (what the job learns first at the bottom, what it learns later above it), then the MP bar, the progress bar, CDs, Defensive CDs and Role Actions, each one hanging from the one above. It applies to new installs and to the Job setup of each job. Added: the vanilla layout is the default of new installs: frames, target of target, focus, progress bars, enfeeblements and the General group are anchored to each other as in the screenshots, nothing is locked, and the global cooldown bar is off. Changed: the Limit Break gauge is a bit thicker by default. Added: the Viewing Cutscene icon of a party member shows centered above their head when their bar is not drawn, and goes back to its place when it is.
